note: dHMN by definition presents with predominantly motor axonal neuropathy without prominent objective sensory loss; significant sensory involvement reclassifies the phenotype toward CMT2.

evidence.text: dHMN patients, including those with SPTAN1 variants, manifest lower limb motor deficits without significant sensory impairment, aligning with the standard distinction between dHMN and sensory-motor neuropathies.

evidence.text: Hereditary motor neuropathies are defined primarily by length-dependent axonal degeneration of lower motor neurons, distinguishing them clinically and mechanistically from Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.

source.title: The expanding genetic landscape of hereditary motor neuropathies
source.quote: Hereditary motor neuropathies are clinically and genetically diverse disorders characterized by length-dependent axonal degeneration of lower motor neurons.
